record.paper_title: Open Problem: Average-Case Hardness of Hypergraphic Planted Clique Detection
record.context_brief: Equivalence of HPC and PC detection
record.original_question: At the threshold kappa = O(N^(1/2 - tau)) for tau > 0, what is the precise computational-hardness relationship between hypergraphic planted clique detection and ordinary planted clique detection? Because fixing d - 2 indices of the adjacency tensor of a d-hypergraph and varying the remaining two gives an adjacency matrix corresponding to a planted clique detection problem, HPC detection is no harder than PC detection; is HPC strictly easier than PC detection, or can one prove a randomized polynomial-time reduction from PC detection to HPC detection showing that the two detection problems are equivalently hard at this threshold?

evidence.quote: what is relationship between HPC detection and PC detection

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer $d \geq 3$ and a parameter $\tau > 0$. For a positive integer $N$, define two distributions on $d$-uniform hypergraphs with vertex set $[N]$:

- (Null) $H_0$: the Erdős–Rényi $d$-uniform random hypergraph in which every $d$-subset of $[N]$ is independently present as a hyperedge with probability $1/2$.
- (Planted) $H_1$: first choose uniformly at random a subset $K \subseteq [N]$ of size $\kappa = \kappa(N)$; sample a random hypergraph as in $H_0$; then add every $d$-subset of $K$ as a hyperedge (so $K$ becomes a "hyperclique").

The hypergraphic planted clique (HPC) detection problem at clique size $\kappa$ asks for a (randomized) polynomial-time test that distinguishes $H_0$ from $H_1$ with vanishing total error as $N \to \infty$.

The (ordinary) planted clique (PC) detection problem is the case $d = 2$: distinguish $G(N, 1/2)$ from $G(N, 1/2)$ with a planted clique on $\kappa$ vertices.

Consider the threshold regime $\kappa = O(N^{1/2 - \tau})$. By fixing any $d-2$ coordinates of the adjacency tensor of a $d$-hypergraph and letting the remaining two vary, one obtains the adjacency matrix of a graph distributed exactly as a PC instance (with the same planted vertex set); hence HPC detection is no harder than PC detection.

Determine the precise computational relationship between HPC detection and PC detection in this regime. Specifically: is HPC detection strictly easier than PC detection (i.e., does there exist a randomized polynomial-time algorithm solving HPC detection at clique size $\kappa = O(N^{1/2-\tau})$ even when no such algorithm exists for PC detection at the same scale), or does there exist a randomized polynomial-time reduction from PC detection to HPC detection establishing that the two problems are equivalently hard at this threshold?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to still be open. Subsequent work on planted hyperclique detection (including recent 2026 work on planted clique detection from the hypergraph adjacency matrix) acknowledges that tight computational lower bounds remain open and does not provide a randomized polynomial-time reduction from PC to HPC at the N^(1/2-tau) threshold. The one-direction reduction (HPC no harder than PC) remains the only proven relationship.
